title: The autopilot manager rehearses one full tick on a scratch sprint, and a runbook says how to start it
goal: python3 _tools/autopilot_rehearse.py runs one manager tick end to end in a throwaway clone with a stubbed claude: it files a scratch planned sprint of two trivial items, selfchecks, starts the sprint through an autopilot-answered start gate with its research done, launches a runner, sees both items land, runs bounds stop, writes the digest and leaves no orphan process or worktree, printing 'rehearse: ok (N steps)' and exiting 1 naming the failed step; a test named autopilot_rehearse plants a failure at each step. kb/_self/backlog.md gets a section 'Starting the autopilot' with the exact commands (a manager session, /loop 15m /kb-autopilot, selfcheck first, where the digest and the stalled list are read, how to stop it) so the operator can test it.
